item.title: US Consumer Sentiment Slips to Five-Month Low on Inflation
item.description:
Oct 23rd, 2026
US Consumer Sentiment Slips to Five-Month Low on Inflation
US consumer sentiment edged down to a five-month low in October as high prices and rising interest rates depressed morale. The University of Michigan’s final sentiment index eased to 48 from 48.1 in September, according to the survey released Friday. Even so, that was an improvement from the preliminary reading and topped all estimates in a Bloomberg survey of economists. Joanne Hsu, University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers Director joins to discuss.

French bond markets suffered a historic bout of turbulence this week as political unrest exacerbates concerns over the country’s public finances.
The premium that investors demand to hold French 10-year debt over Germany’s jumped by 29 basis points this week, the second biggest rise on records dating back to 1990, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. The yield gap now stands around 1.7 percentage points, more than double the level from May.

A resurgence in oil prices dragged down stocks and bonds, stoking concerns about inflation just days ahead of the Federal Reserve decision on interest rates.
Brent crude topped $116 as a flare-up in Middle East violence threatened global supplies. The S&P 500 saw back-to-back losses. That’s even as selling pressure on tech firms abated. A gauge of chipmakers rebounded, while still heading toward its longest weekly slide since November. Treasury yields rose after the market’s best day in more than a year.

item.title: Decker Outdoor Tumbles on Guidance; Amex to Cut Workforce | Stock Movers
item.description:
On this episode of Stock Movers:
- Decker Outdoor (DECK) is tumbling after the footwear company cut its net sales guidance for the full year, which also fell short of the consensus estimate. - Kering (KER) shares are slumping after the French luxury-goods company saw further deceleration of third-quarter revenue growth at its key Gucci unit, slower growth in North America as well as persistent weakness in China. - American Express (AXP) shares are moving on news that the company is planning to cut 5% of its global headcount. Chief Executive Officer Steve Squeri told Bloomberg TV that the move will affect about 3,500 jobs. - Moderna (MRNA) plummeted after data on the companies’ widely anticipated melanoma vaccine wasn’t enough to prove to investors that a new era of cancer treatments has arrived. While the results clearly showed the vaccine worked, they weren’t spectacular enough to generate confidence. (Source: Bloomberg)
